national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said India’s 7.8 percent quarterly growth amid global uncertainty reflects its economic strength. He said India has come a long way, from policy paralysis to policy dynamism. Addressing the gathering at the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi, Mr Modi said the world is watching India become the fastest growing major economy. Prime Minister said Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) has given generations of students the opportunity to learn, grow and make a difference over the years. Mr Modi said the college has distinguished itself over the years, making a mark for academic excellence. He termed the alumni of SRCC as very special and ‘the OGs’. The Prime Minister stated that former Finance Minister Arun Jaitley was an alum of SRCC. He said SRCC alumni have left their mark in every sector, from arts to politics. He added that together, 140 crore Indians will make India both Viksit and Aatmanirbhar. The Prime Minister also said that India has come a long way from policy paralysis to policy dynamism. Mr. Modi also lauded the students of SRCC for taking its glory to the global stage. Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, in his speech, praised SRCC for maintaing its high standard over the years. He said today India is the third largest Start Up ecosystem under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi. He said there is requirement of skilled human resources in the global market. The Minister termed it an opportunity for the young population. Earlier this evening, Prime Minister Modi traveled by the Delhi Metro as he headed to SRCC to participate in the college’s centenary celebrations.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 58 Over 500 investors, finance ministers and business leaders to attend inaugural iBRICS Summit
national_raw_news.content: More than 500 institutional investors, finance ministers and business leaders will participate in the inaugural iBRICS Summit, on the sidelines of BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 12th and 13th of this month. The two-day summit is designed to connect sovereign capital with bankable infrastructure, energy, and digital capacity projects across 21 BRICS member states and partner nations. Sovereign wealth funds, pension funds and family offices attending the iBRICS Summit manage a total wealth of 1 trillion US Dollars. They will discuss cross-border investments, non-dollar settlements and payment systems among BRICS economies. Discussions are also expected on linking national fast-payment systems such as India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Brazil’s Pix, along with interoperability between central bank digital currencies. The summit comes at a critical juncture as BRICS economies adapt to shifting trade dynamics, US tariff pressures, and high dollar-clearing costs. The meeting is intended to connect institutional capital with infrastructure, energy and digital projects across BRICS member and partner countries. As BRICS Chair 2026, India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Summit will bring together leaders of BRICS Member and Partner Countries as well as Outreach Invitees. India’s BRICS Chairship is guided by the theme: “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting the Prime Minister’s vision of a people-centric approach rooted in the spirit of “Humanity First”.
